summary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment limiting federal expenditures each year to the average annual receipts over the prior three years (adjusted for population and inflation, excluding debt payments and borrowing), allowing overrides only by two-thirds roll-call votes in each House or during declared wars, and requiring two-thirds approval for new or increased taxes.

scores.thoughts: This bill proposes a constitutional amendment to limit federal expenditures, directly aiming to reduce or control government spending by tying it to average past receipts. This is a central theme of the bill.

The bill includes a provision requiring a two-thirds vote in both chambers of Congress to levy a new tax or increase an existing one, making it harder to raise taxes. This is a significant component of the proposed amendment.
By limiting federal expenditures to average receipts, the bill aims to prevent deficit spending and thus reduce the national debt. This is a primary objective of the proposed fiscal restraint.
